title: SwiftUI app and view lifecycle (App, Scene, onAppear, .task)
summary: A SwiftUI app starts from an `App` struct with one or more `Scene`s. Views get `onAppear`/`onDisappear` and `.task` (async work that is cancelled automatically when the view goes away).
body: **In simple words:** `@main struct MyApp: App` replaces the old AppDelegate as the entry point. Its `body` returns scenes like `WindowGroup`. Each window shows a root view.

**App state:** read `@Environment(\.scenePhase)` to know if the app is `.active`, `.inactive` or `.background` - save data when going to background. You can still plug in an AppDelegate with `@UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor` for push tokens or SDK setup.

**View events:** `onAppear` / `onDisappear` run when a view enters or leaves the screen. `.task { }` starts async work when the view appears and **cancels it when the view disappears** - the best place to load data. `.task(id: value)` restarts the work when `value` changes (e.g. a search query). `onChange(of:)` reacts to a value change.
**Important difference:** a view's `init` and `body` can run many times; `onAppear` runs when it appears, not when it is created. Do not start network calls in `init`.
**Lists:** in a `List`/`LazyVStack`, rows appear and disappear while scrolling, so `onAppear` can fire many times - good for pagination ("load more when the last row appears").
keyPoints: `.task` = async work tied to view lifetime, auto-cancelled; `.task(id:)` restarts on change.
`init`/`body` run often; never put side effects there.
`onAppear` on the last row is a simple pagination trigger.

code.caption: App entry and data loading

mistakes: Starting work in a view `init` (runs on every parent redraw).
Using `onAppear { Task { ... } }` and never cancelling - prefer `.task`.
followups: **Where do you handle push notification registration in SwiftUI?** In an AppDelegate connected with `@UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor`.
**When is `onAppear` called more than once?** When the view leaves and comes back, e.g. tabs, navigation pop, lazy list scrolling.
